The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to them: "Your profession of Islam will not be accepted from you until you emigrate." So they set out intending for Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and fought them; some of them were killed and some of them escaped. Then Allah revealed these two verses [[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Dur (6/449) as belonging to 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (20/129), Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Juraij said: it was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who was tortured for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic [[Ibn al-Mundhir related it from Ibn Juraij from Ibn 'Umayr and others. It was also related by Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn 'Asakir. See: al-Dur al-Manthur 6/450, Zad al-Masir 6/254.]]. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Mihja' ibn 'Abd Allah, the freed slave of 'Umar, who was the first of the Muslims to be killed on the day of Badr. (393). The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (127): "al-Tha'labi mentioned it from Muqatil..." then he said: "Its chain to Muqatil is at the beginning of his book. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 3–4:

﴿And We certainly tested those before them﴾, meaning the prophets and the believers. Some of them were sawn in two with a saw, and some were killed. The Children of Israel were tested with Pharaoh, who would subject them to ﴿a terrible torment﴾ (66/b). ﴿So Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful﴾ in their saying "We believe", ﴿and He will surely make evident the liars﴾. Allah knew about them before the testing. The meaning of the verse: Allah will surely make manifest the truthful from the liars until what He knows is brought into existence. Muqatil said: "Allah will surely see." It was also said: "Allah will surely distinguish", like His saying: ﴿that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾, meaning shirk, ﴿that they will outrun Us﴾, that they will overpower Us and escape Us, so that We are not able to take retribution against them, ﴿evil is what they judge﴾. How wrong they were to judge when they thought this.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 5–8:

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) and Muqatil said: whoever fears the Resurrection and the Reckoning. Al-rajaʾ (hope) here carries the meaning of fear (al-khawf). Saʿid ibn Jubayr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: whoever aspires to the reward of Allah. ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah is coming﴾ meaning: what Allah has promised of reward and punishment. Muqatil said: meaning, the Day of Resurrection is surely coming. The sense of the verse is that whoever fears Allah or hopes in Him should prepare for it, and should work for that Day, as He said: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds" [al-Kahf: 110], ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

﴿And whoever strives, strives only for himself﴾: his reward is for himself. "Jihad" (struggle): it is patience upon hardship, and it occurs in war, and it may also occur in opposing the self (mukhalafat al-nafs).

﴿Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾: from their deeds and their acts of worship.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾: We will nullify them, meaning that they will become as if they had never been committed. Takfir (expiation) is the removal of an evil deed by a good deed. ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, according to their best deeds, which is obedience. It was also said: We will give them more than what they did, and better, as He said: "Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like" [al-Anʿam: 160].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾: that is, dutifulness toward them and tenderness to them. Its meaning: We enjoined upon man that he do toward his parents what is good. This verse, and the one in Surah Luqman (verse 15) and al-Ahqaf (verse 15), were revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) – he is Saʿd ibn Malik, Abu Ishaq al-Zuhri, and his mother was Hamnah bint Abi Sufyan ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams – when he embraced Islam. He was among the foremost early believers, and he was dutiful to his mother. His mother said to him: "What is this religion you have invented? By Allah, I will neither eat nor drink until you return to what you were upon, or I die, and you will be reproached for it forever, and it will be said: 'O slayer of his mother!'" Then she remained a day and a night without eating or drinking [and without seeking shade], so in the morning she was exhausted. Then she remained another day without eating or drinking, and Saʿd came to her and said: "O mother, even if you had a hundred souls and they departed one by one, I would not abandon my religion. So eat, and if you wish, do not eat." When she despaired of him, she ate and drank. Then Allah revealed this verse, commanding him to be dutiful to his parents and kind to them, but not to obey them in shirk. This is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ [[Narrated by al-Wahidi (p. 394) and al-Tha'labi; al-Waqidi related it without a chain. The story is in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, in a different wording, in the Book of the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtue of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him), no. (1748): 4/1877. See also: al-Sahih al-Musnad min Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wadiʿi, p. 113.]]. And it has come in a hadith: "There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to Allah" [[Narrated by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/44, from the narration of al-Nawwas ibn Samʿan, and by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir. It was also narrated by al-Tayalisi (p. 115) and Imam Ahmad: 5/66, and al-Hakim authenticated it: 3/443, from the narration of ʿImran ibn Husayn. Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Ibn Masʿud.]]. Then He threatened with the return to Him, saying: ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾: I will inform you of your good and bad deeds, and then I will recompense you for them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 9–10:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾ Among the company of the righteous, who are the prophets and the saints (awliya'). It is also said: into the abode of the righteous, which is Paradise.

That is, he panics at the torment of the people and does not endure it, so he obeys the people just as one who fears His punishment obeys Allah. This is the view of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, who said: it is the hypocrite who, when harmed for the sake of Allah, turns back from the religion and disbelieves.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 11–12:

﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe﴾: they were truthful and remained steadfast in Islam at the time of trial. ﴿And He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾: by abandoning Islam when trials befall them. They differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning people who professed belief with their tongues; when a trial from people or a calamity affecting their own selves befell them, they succumbed to temptation [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in al-Asbab, p. 395; al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/452) to al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]. Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: It was revealed concerning those whom the polytheists took out to Badr [[See: al-Tabari 20/123; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 396.]], and they are the ones concerning whom it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [al-Nisa: 97]. Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the group whom the polytheists sent back to Makkah [[See: al-Tabari 20/133.]]. Al-Sha'bi said: These first ten verses of the surah up to this point are Madani, and the remaining surahs are Makki [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Nahhas: 5/214; al-Tabari also narrated it from Qatadah in the same place. Refer to footnote (1) at the beginning of the surah, p. 231.]].

﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed: Follow our way﴾. Mujahid said: This is the statement of the Makkan disbelievers to those among them who believed. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Abu Sufyan said it to those among the Quraysh who believed: "Follow our way": our religion and the creed of our fathers, and we will bear every consequence from Allah that befalls you. That is His saying: ﴿and let us carry your sins﴾ (your burdens). Al-Farra' said: the wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a conditional reward [[He said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (2/314): it is an imperative carrying the sense of a conditional response, and he recited the verse of Dathar ibn Shaybān al-Namari: "So I said: call, and I will call, for the more fitting ... to a voice is that two callers call."]]. Its meaning is: if you follow our way, we will bear your sins. It is like His saying: ﴿let the sea cast it onto the shore﴾ [Taha: 39]. It was also said: it is a jussive on the imperative, as though they commanded themselves with this, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuted them, saying: ﴿And they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars﴾ in what they said about bearing their sins.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 29, verses 13–17:**

﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾: the burdens of their own deeds which they committed themselves. ﴿And burdens along with their burdens﴾: that is, the burdens of those whom they misled and turned away from the way of Allah, along with their own burdens. A parallel to this is the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge" [al-Nahl: 25].

﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾: a questioning of rebuke and reproach.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them﴾ and they drowned, ﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They were polytheists."

﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ark﴾, meaning from the drowning. ﴿And We made it﴾, meaning the ark, ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a lesson, ﴿for the worlds﴾. For it remained upon al-Judi for a long period. It was also said: We made their punishment by drowning a lesson.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: [67/a] Noah was sent at the age of forty, and he remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty years. He lived after the flood sixty years, until people multiplied and spread. His lifespan was one thousand and fifty years.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Abraham﴾, that is, And We sent Abraham, ﴿when he said to his people: Worship Allah and fear Him﴾, obey Allah and be in awe of Him, ﴿that is better for you, if you only knew﴾.

﴿You only worship besides Allah idols﴾, images, ﴿and you invent a falsehood﴾, you say a lie. Mujahid said: You fashion idols with your hands and then name them gods. ﴿Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision﴾, they cannot provide sustenance for you. ﴿So seek﴾, then ask, ﴿from Allah the provision, and worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 29, verses 18–22:**

﴿And if you deny, then nations before you have denied,﴾ like ʿAd, Thamud and others, and they were destroyed. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾

﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation?﴾ How He creates them originally: a drop (nutfah), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah). ﴿Then He will repeat it﴾ in the Hereafter at the Resurrection. ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾

﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe how He began creation.﴾ Look at their dwellings and their remains, and how He began their creation. ﴿Then Allah will bring about the final creation.﴾ That is, then Allah, who created it, will bring it into being a second time after death. Just as originating it was not beyond Him, re-creating it is not beyond Him. Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read النَّشَأَةَ with a fatha on the shin and a long vowel (مَمْدُودَةً) wherever it occurs, while the others read it with a sukun on the shin and a short vowel (مَقْصُورَةً). Its parallel is الرَّأْفَةُ and الرَّآفَةُ.

﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ Turned back (tuqlabun): you will be sent back.

﴿You cannot escape [Him] on the earth or in the heaven.﴾ If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying "nor in the heaven," when the address is to the children of Adam, who are not in the heaven?

Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "nor whoever is in the heaven can escape," like the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:

*"So whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of Allah*
*and praises him and supports him, they are equal."*

He intended: "whoever praises him and whoever supports him," so he omitted مَنْ (whoever), meaning: the people of the earth cannot overpower Him on the earth, nor the people of the heaven in the heaven.

Qutrub said: its meaning is "You cannot escape on the earth or in the heaven, even if you were in it," like a man saying: "So-and-so does not escape me here, nor in Basra," meaning: nor in Basra even if he were there.

﴿And you have no protector other than Allah, nor any helper.﴾ That is: no protector who can shield you from Me, and no helper who can save you from My punishment.

﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Scripture﴾. It is said: Allah did not send any prophet after Abraham except from his progeny. ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾, which is the good praise; so all the people of the religions take him as their guide (walla, "to take as a guide or ally"). Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read "ā'innakum" (أَئِنَّكُمْ) with the interrogative (istifham, "question particle"). The rest read it without the interrogative, and they all agreed on the interrogative for the second word, ﴿you come to the foul deed﴾, which is coming to men, ﴿that no one among the worlds has preceded you in﴾.

﴿Do you indeed come to men and cut off the way and commit in your gatherings the evil?﴾ That is because they used to commit the foul deed with those travelers who passed by them, so people abandoned passing by them. It was also said: "you cut off the path of offspring by preferring men over women." ﴿And you commit in your gatherings the evil (al-munkar)﴾. Al-nadi, al-nada, and al-muntada: the assembly of a people and the place of their conversation. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu al-Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi informed us, my maternal grandfather Abu al-Hasan al-Mahmudi informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah informed us, that Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to them: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Abu Salih, the freedman of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, [from Umm Hani'] [[Omitted from "a".]] who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying: ﴿and you commit in your gatherings the evil﴾. I said: What is the evil (al-munkar) that they used to commit? He said: "They used to pelt the people of the roads with pebbles and mock them." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir of Surah al-'Ankabut: 9/49–50, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah from Simak." Al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim): 2/409, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. It was also narrated by Imam Ahmad: 6/341, and al-Tabari: 20/145.

Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr (6/460): "It was narrated by al-Firyabi, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi who graded it hasan, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in his book "al-Samt," Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Shashi in his Musnad, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in "al-Shu'ab," and Ibn Asakir."]].

It is also narrated that they used to sit in their assemblies, and each man among them had a bowl containing pebbles; when a passerby came by them, they pelted him, and whoever hit him had the better claim to him. It was also said: he would take what was with him and sodomize him, and fine him three dirhams, and they had a judge for this. Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: they used to break wind openly in their assemblies [[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Nahhas: 5/223; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/461; Zad al-Masir: 6/269.]]. Mujahid said: some of them used to have intercourse with one another in their assemblies [[Attributed by al-Suyuti (6/461) to al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Kharaʼiti in "Masawi al-Akhlaq."]]. From Abdullah ibn Salam, he said: some of them used to spit on others. From Makhul, he said: among the manners of the people of Lot were chewing gum, dyeing the fingers with henna, untying the waistwrap, whistling, pelting with pebbles, and sodomy [[This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/461; Zad al-Masir: 6/269. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his commentary on this verse (3/412): "That is, they commit what is unbecoming of words and deeds in their assemblies where they gather; none of them denounces any of that to another." ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said﴾, when Lot denounced to them the abominations they were committing, ﴿"Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are among the truthful"﴾, mocking him, meaning that the punishment would descend upon us. Thereupon...

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 33–37:

﴿When Our messengers came to Lut﴾, he thought they were human, ﴿he was distressed on their account and felt helplessly constrained by their coming﴾, ﴿and they said, "Do not fear"﴾ for your people against us, ﴿"nor grieve"﴾ over our destroying them, ﴿"we will deliver you and your family, except your wife, who will be among those who remain behind."﴾ Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub recited "مُنْجُوكَ" (munjūka) with light stress (takhfif). The others recited it with emphatic stress (tashdid).

﴿"We are going to send down"﴾ Ibn Amir recited it with emphatic stress, and the others with light stress, ﴿"upon the people of this town a punishment"﴾, meaning a torment, ﴿"from the sky."﴾ Muqatil said: it was sinking into the earth and a rain of stones (al-khasf wa al-hasb). ﴿"Because they were defiant."﴾

Ibn Abbas said: the clear sign is the traces of their ruined dwellings. Qatadah said: it is the stones with which they were destroyed, which God preserved until the early generations of this community reached them. This is the commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 29, verses 38–40:

﴿And 'Ad and Thamud﴾, that is, and We destroyed 'Ad and Thamud. ﴿And it has become clear to you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿from their dwellings﴾, their homes at al-Hijr and in Yemen. ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear fair to them and barred them from the path﴾, from the path of truth. ﴿And they were discerning﴾ (*mustabsirin*). Muqatil, al-Kalbi and Qatadah said: they were self-satisfied in their religion and their misguidance, thinking that they were upon guidance while they were upon falsehood. [[This is what al-Tabari preferred: 20/150.]] The meaning is that they considered themselves to be discerning. Al-Farra' said: they were intelligent people possessing insight. [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 2/213. Al-Qurtubi also preferred this: 13/344.]]

﴿And Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman﴾, that is, We destroyed these. ﴿And Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs﴾, with evidence. ﴿But they were arrogant in the land, and they were not ones who could escape﴾, that is, they could not escape from Our punishment.

﴿So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles﴾, referring to the people of Lot. The word "al-hasib" (*al-haasib*) refers to the wind that carries *al-hasba'* (*al-hasbaa'*), which are small pebbles. ﴿And among them were those seized by the Cry﴾, meaning Thamud. ﴿And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾, meaning Qarun and his companions. ﴿And among them were those whom We drowned﴾, meaning the people of Noah, and Pharaoh and his people. ﴿And it was not Allah who wronged them, but they were wronging themselves﴾. [[The Exalted says: Allah did not destroy these nations, whom He destroyed, for the sins of others, thereby wronging them by destroying them without deserving it. Rather, He destroyed them for their own sins and their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His blessings upon them, despite the continuous succession of His kindness to them and the abundance of His favours toward them. ﴿The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾ means: the idols, who hope for their support and benefit. ﴿Is like the spider that takes a house﴾ for itself, to which it retreats. Indeed, the spider's house is extremely weak and flimsy. It does not protect it from heat or cold. Likewise, the idols possess no power to benefit or harm their worshippers.

﴿And indeed, the weakest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon besides Him, of any thing. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ The people of Basra and 'Asim read "yad'una" (they call) with the letter ya', referring to the nations mentioned before it. The others read it with the letter ta'.

﴿And these are the parables﴾: the likenesses and examples. A mathal (parable) is a widely circulated saying that conveys the comparison of one thing to another. He means the parables of the Qur'an, by which the states of the disbelievers of this nation are compared to the states of the disbelievers of earlier nations. ﴿We set them forth﴾ means We explain them. ﴿For the people﴾: Muqatil said, "For the disbelievers of Makkah." ﴿And none understands them except the knowledgeable﴾ means: none truly comprehends the parables except the scholars who understand from Allah. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Ibn Fanjawayh informed me; Ibn Barzah informed us; al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah informed us; Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar informed us; 'Abbad ibn Kathir informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' and Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for the people, and none understands them except the knowledgeable.﴾ He said: "The knowledgeable one is he who understands from Allah, so he acts in His obedience and avoids His wrath." [[Narrated by Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar in his book "al-Aql" (The Intellect), and through him al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad (Bughyat al-Baherth, no. 1030), from the hadith of Jabir. Also by al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi in their tafsirs, and al-Wahidi through the route of al-Harith. Ibn al-Jawzi included it in "al-Mawdu'at" (The Fabricated Reports), and Ibn 'Iraq in "Tanzih al-Shari'ah 'an al-Akhbar al-Shani'ah wa al-Mawdu'ah" (Purifying the Shari'ah from Shameful and Fabricated Reports). The hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in "al-Matalib al-'Aliyah" (3/215) among the hadiths from Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar's book "al-Aql," and said: al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah included them in his Musnad, and they are all fabricated; nothing from them is authentic. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 127; al-Matalib al-'Aliyah, 3/213, 214 and 216; al-Fath al-Samawi by al-Manawi, 2/896–897; Tanzih al-Shari'ah by Ibn 'Iraq, 1/214.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 44–45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, meaning: for the truth, and to manifest the truth. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, in their creation, ﴿is a sign﴾, an indication ﴿for the believers﴾ of His power and His oneness.

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾. Al-fahsha' (immorality) is what is ugly of deeds, and al-munkar (wrongdoing) is what is not recognized in the Shari'ah. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: In prayer there is a limit and a restraint from the disobedience of Allah. Whoever his prayer does not command him to good, and does not forbid him from wrongdoing, his prayer increases him in nothing from Allah except distance.[[The report from Ibn Mas'ud was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and its narrators are trustworthy, and Ahmad narrated it in al-Zuhd. As for the report from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Tabari narrated it: 20/155, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir from the narration of al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyib from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf (companion's statement). Al-Tabarani, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet). Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is trustworthy but a mudallis (one who conceals defects in his chains). Ibn Hajar said: There is also a report on this from Ibn 'Umar, narrated by al-Daraqutni in "Gharib Malik", and its chain includes Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri. Ibn Hibban said: It is not permissible to take it as evidence; he narrates from Malik what has no basis. Thus the report is weak when traced to the Prophet, and sound when stopped at Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.

See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/258; al-Kafi al-Shaf pp. (127–128); Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah: 2/414–415, no. (985); al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/464 and 465; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/415–416. Furthermore, it is the nature of prayer, when a Muslim performs it and fulfills its obligations and limits as they should be, and reflects upon it and upon what he recites of the Qur'an, that it restrains its performer from immorality and wrongdoing. This is because of what it contains of reciting the Qur'an, which includes admonition. Prayer engages the whole body of the one praying. When he enters his prayer, becomes humble and submissive to his Lord, remembers that he stands before Him, that He is watching him and sees him, his soul becomes disposed to that, humbled, the awareness of Allah the Exalted pervades it, and its awe appears upon his limbs. If something contrary to that occurs or emerges from him, his prayer will not increase him in distance from Allah. And the one who prays is better than the one who does not pray. See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/348.]].

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Whoever his prayer does not restrain from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer is a burden upon him.[[Al-Tabari narrated it from al-Hasan as a mawquf: 20/155, and by another route as a marfu' mursal (a report with a missing companion), and from Qatadah as a mawquf statement from his own words. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf (128): It was narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Shu'ab" from the mursal of al-Hasan. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/466.]] It is related from Anas who said: There was a young man from the Ansar who prayed the five prayers with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he would leave no immorality without committing it. His condition was described to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed his prayer will restrain him one day." And he did not delay until he repented and his condition became good.[[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. (128): I have not found it. Al-Wali al-Iraqi said: I have not come across it. (al-Fath al-Samawi: 2/897). When such a statement is made, and similar ones, by one of the known hadith scholars, and no hadith scholar after him has objected to it, it suffices for ruling the hadith as fabricated. See the introduction of Shaykh 'Abd al-Fattah Abu Ghuddah to the book "al-Masnu' fi Ma'rifat al-Hadith al-Mawdu'" by al-Qari, pp. (25–27).]] Ibn 'Awn said: The meaning of the verse is that prayer restrains its performer from immorality and wrongdoing for as long as he is in it.[[Ibn Kathir related this statement from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman: 3/416, and related its meaning at length from Ibn 'Awn; it is also the view of al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj, as in al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/153 and al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/226. Ibn 'Atiyyah rejected this view, saying: This is a non-Arabic (weak) view, and where is this from what Anas ibn Malik narrated (as in the previous note)?]]

It was also said: By prayer He meant the Qur'an, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾ [al-Isra': 110], meaning: in your recitation. And He meant that he recites the Qur'an in the prayer, so the Qur'an restrains him from immorality and wrongdoing.[[Al-Tabari narrated it from Ibn 'Umar: 20/154. He preferred the first view: that prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing. If someone says: How can prayer restrain from immorality and wrongdoing if it does not mean what is recited in it?

It is said: It restrains the one who is in it, by coming between him and committing abominations, because his occupation with it cuts him off from occupation with wrongdoing. That is why Ibn Mas'ud said: Whoever does not obey his prayer will not increase from Allah except distance. His obedience to it is his establishing it with its limits, and in his obedience to it there is a restraint from immorality and wrongdoing.]] We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: We were informed by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh, who said: We were informed by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, who said: We were informed by 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd, who said: We were informed by Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed a man recites the Qur'an all night, then in the morning he steals." He said: "His recitation will restrain him."[[Narrated by al-Bazzar through the route of Ziyad al-Bakka'i, and Abu Ya'la through the route of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, both from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Jabir. Al-Bazzar said: It was disputed concerning al-A'mash: it was said that he also narrated it from Abu Sufyan from Jabir. Al-Haythami said: Its narrators are trustworthy. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (128), Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/258, al-Fath al-Samawi 2/897–898.]]

And in another narration it was said: O Messenger of Allah, indeed so-and-so prays by day and steals by night. He said: "Indeed his prayer will deter him."[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad from Abu Hurayrah: 2/447, with the wording "...what he says will restrain him," and by al-Bazzar, Ishaq, and Abu Ya'la, all through the route of al-A'mash from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah. Al-Haythami said: its narrators are those of the sound (collection). See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (128), al-Majma' 2/258, al-Fath al-Samawi: 2/897.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, meaning: the remembrance of Allah is the best of acts of obedience. Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri informed us, who said: Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran informed us in Baghdad, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Safwan al-Bardha'i informed us, who said: Abu Bakr 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya informed us, who said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf Abu 'Ali al-Darir informed us, who said: Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, mawla of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu Tajrabah, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy, striking their necks and they striking yours?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on the best of deeds: 9/317–318, and he said: some of them narrated this hadith from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id in this same chain, and some of them narrated it from him as mursal. Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Adab, chapter on the virtue of remembrance, no. (3790): 2/1245, and al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/496, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Imam Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta': 1/211 as a mawquf report from Abu al-Darda'. Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/477. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/16, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/467; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/73.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, who said: Abu Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, who said: Abu al-Aswad informed us, who said: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked: Which of the servants is greatest in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Those who remember Allah much." They said: O Messenger of Allah, and what of the one who fights in the way of Allah? He said: "Even if he struck the disbelievers and polytheists with his sword until it broke or was dyed with blood, the one who remembers Allah much would still be greater in rank than him."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat: 9/315–316, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith, we only know it from the hadith of Darraj." Also by Imam Ahmad: 3/75, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/17. Al-Mundhiri in al-Targhib pointed to its weakness and said: al-Bayhaqi narrated it abridged: 2/396, and in it is Ibn Lahi'ah, who became confused, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]]

It is also related that a Bedouin said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the deeds is best? He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Abd Allah ibn Bisr in al-Da'awat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of remembrance: 9/314–315, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/495, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Hibban p. (576) in Mawarid al-Zam'an, Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/188, 190, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 6/111, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/16. Its chain is sound.]]

We were informed by Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani, who said: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, who said: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Qushayri informed us, who said: Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Aysh informed us, who said: Yazid, that is Ibn Zuray', informed us, who said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim informed us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was traveling on the road to Makkah, and he passed a mountain called Jumdan, and he said: "Proceed, this is Jumdan; the mufarridun (those who are single-minded) have outpaced." They said: "And who are the mufarridun, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The men and women who remember Allah much."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on urging the remembrance of Allah, no. (1676): 4/2062.]]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us, who said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam informed us, who said: al-Nadr narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aghharr say: I bear witness concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "No people sit remembering Allah except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on the virtue of gathering to recite the Qur'an, no. (2700): 4/2074, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/10–11.]] Some people said: The meaning of His saying, "And the remembrance of Allah is greater," is: Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.[[Al-Suyuti attributed it (6/466) to al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman". It is also the view of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. Ibn 'Atiyyah (12/227–228) preferred that the meaning is: "And the remembrance of Allah is greater" absolutely, i.e., it is what forbids immorality and wrongdoing. The part of it performed in prayer does this, and likewise it does so outside prayer, because restraint only comes from a remembrance that is aware of being watched...]] It is also the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.[[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/467.]] It is also related with a marfu' chain from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ.[[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami, 6/466; his attribution to al-Daylami indicates weakness.]] 'Ata' said concerning His saying: "Indeed prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater," he said: The remembrance of Allah is greater than that any disobedience should remain alongside it.

﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾. 'Ata' said: He means nothing is hidden from Him.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Whoever his prayer does not restrain from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer is a burden upon him.[[Al-Tabari narrated it from al-Hasan as a mawquf: 20/155, and by another route as a marfu' mursal (a report with a missing companion), and from Qatadah as a mawquf statement from his own words. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf (128): It was narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Shu'ab" from the mursal of al-Hasan. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/466.]] It is related from Anas who said: There was a young man from the Ansar who prayed the five prayers with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he would leave no immorality without committing it. His condition was described to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Indeed his prayer will restrain him one day." And he did not delay until he repented and his condition became good.[[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. (128): I have not found it. Al-Wali al-Iraqi said: I have not come across it. (al-Fath al-Samawi: 2/897). When such a statement is made, and similar ones, by one of the known hadith scholars, and no hadith scholar after him has objected to it, it suffices for ruling the hadith as fabricated. See the introduction of Shaykh 'Abd al-Fattah Abu Ghuddah to the book "al-Masnu' fi Ma'rifat al-Hadith al-Mawdu'" by al-Qari, pp. (25–27).]] Ibn 'Awn said: The meaning of the verse is that prayer restrains its performer from immorality and wrongdoing for as long as he is in it.[[Ibn Kathir related this statement from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman: 3/416, and related its meaning at length from Ibn 'Awn; it is also the view of al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj, as in al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/153 and al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 12/226. Ibn 'Atiyyah rejected this view, saying: This is a non-Arabic (weak) view, and where is this from what Anas ibn Malik narrated (as in the previous note)?]]

It was also said: By prayer He meant the Qur'an, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾ [al-Isra': 110], meaning: in your recitation. And He meant that he recites the Qur'an in the prayer, so the Qur'an restrains him from immorality and wrongdoing.[[Al-Tabari narrated it from Ibn 'Umar: 20/154. He preferred the first view: that prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing. If someone says: How can prayer restrain from immorality and wrongdoing if it does not mean what is recited in it?

It is said: It restrains the one who is in it, by coming between him and committing abominations, because his occupation with it cuts him off from occupation with wrongdoing. That is why Ibn Mas'ud said: Whoever does not obey his prayer will not increase from Allah except distance. His obedience to it is his establishing it with its limits, and in his obedience to it there is a restraint from immorality and wrongdoing.]] We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: We were informed by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh, who said: We were informed by Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, who said: We were informed by 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd, who said: We were informed by Qays ibn al-Rabi', from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed a man recites the Qur'an all night, then in the morning he steals." He said: "His recitation will restrain him."[[Narrated by al-Bazzar through the route of Ziyad al-Bakka'i, and Abu Ya'la through the route of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, both from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Jabir. Al-Bazzar said: It was disputed concerning al-A'mash: it was said that he also narrated it from Abu Sufyan from Jabir. Al-Haythami said: Its narrators are trustworthy. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (128), Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2/258, al-Fath al-Samawi 2/897–898.]]

And in another narration it was said: O Messenger of Allah, indeed so-and-so prays by day and steals by night. He said: "Indeed his prayer will deter him."[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad from Abu Hurayrah: 2/447, with the wording "...what he says will restrain him," and by al-Bazzar, Ishaq, and Abu Ya'la, all through the route of al-A'mash from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah. Al-Haythami said: its narrators are those of the sound (collection). See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (128), al-Majma' 2/258, al-Fath al-Samawi: 2/897.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, meaning: the remembrance of Allah is the best of acts of obedience. Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri informed us, who said: Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran informed us in Baghdad, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Safwan al-Bardha'i informed us, who said: Abu Bakr 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya informed us, who said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf Abu 'Ali al-Darir informed us, who said: Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, mawla of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu Tajrabah, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy, striking their necks and they striking yours?" They said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on the best of deeds: 9/317–318, and he said: some of them narrated this hadith from 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id in this same chain, and some of them narrated it from him as mursal. Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Adab, chapter on the virtue of remembrance, no. (3790): 2/1245, and al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/496, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Imam Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta': 1/211 as a mawquf report from Abu al-Darda'. Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/477. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/16, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/467; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/73.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, who said: Abu Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, who said: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, who said: Abu al-Aswad informed us, who said: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked: Which of the servants is greatest in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection? He said: "Those who remember Allah much." They said: O Messenger of Allah, and what of the one who fights in the way of Allah? He said: "Even if he struck the disbelievers and polytheists with his sword until it broke or was dyed with blood, the one who remembers Allah much would still be greater in rank than him."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat: 9/315–316, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith, we only know it from the hadith of Darraj." Also by Imam Ahmad: 3/75, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/17. Al-Mundhiri in al-Targhib pointed to its weakness and said: al-Bayhaqi narrated it abridged: 2/396, and in it is Ibn Lahi'ah, who became confused, and Darraj's narration from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]]

It is also related that a Bedouin said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the deeds is best? He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Abd Allah ibn Bisr in al-Da'awat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of remembrance: 9/314–315, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route." Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/495, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Hibban p. (576) in Mawarid al-Zam'an, Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/188, 190, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 6/111, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/16. Its chain is sound.]]

We were informed by Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani, who said: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, who said: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Qushayri informed us, who said: Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Aysh informed us, who said: Yazid, that is Ibn Zuray', informed us, who said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim informed us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was traveling on the road to Makkah, and he passed a mountain called Jumdan, and he said: "Proceed, this is Jumdan; the mufarridun (those who are single-minded) have outpaced." They said: "And who are the mufarridun, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The men and women who remember Allah much."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on urging the remembrance of Allah, no. (1676): 4/2062.]]

We were informed by Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us, who said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam informed us, who said: al-Nadr narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aghharr say: I bear witness concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "No people sit remembering Allah except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a, chapter on the virtue of gathering to recite the Qur'an, no. (2700): 4/2074, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/10–11.]] Some people said: The meaning of His saying, "And the remembrance of Allah is greater," is: Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas.[[Al-Suyuti attributed it (6/466) to al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman". It is also the view of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. Ibn 'Atiyyah (12/227–228) preferred that the meaning is: "And the remembrance of Allah is greater" absolutely, i.e., it is what forbids immorality and wrongdoing. The part of it performed in prayer does this, and likewise it does so outside prayer, because restraint only comes from a remembrance that is aware of being watched...]] It is also the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.[[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/467.]] It is also related with a marfu' chain from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ.[[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami, 6/466; his attribution to al-Daylami indicates weakness.]] 'Ata' said concerning His saying: "Indeed prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater," he said: The remembrance of Allah is greater than that any disobedience should remain alongside it.

﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾. 'Ata' said: He means nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 46:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book﴾ — do not dispute with them — ﴿except in a way that is best﴾ — that is, with the Qur'an, calling to God through His signs, and drawing attention to His proofs. And this refers to those among them who accept the jizya (poll tax). ﴿Except those of them who have done wrong﴾ — that is, those who refused to give the jizya and took up war. So argue with them by the sword until they embrace Islam or give the jizya. The implied meaning of the verse is: "except those who have wronged you," because all of them are wrongdoers through disbelief. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are the people of war and those who have no covenant. Qatadah and Muqatil said: it has been abrogated (mansukha) [[See what has preceded: 3/32, note (1); Zad al-Masir: 6/277. And al-Tabari (21/2-3) preferred that the verse is muhkam (not abrogated), since it is not permissible to judge that a ruling of God in His Book is abrogated except with a proof that must be accepted, either from a report or from reason.]] by His saying: "Fight those who do not believe in God" [al-Tawbah: 29].

﴿And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and revealed to you﴾ — he means: if one of them who has accepted the jizya informs you of something from their books, then do not argue with them about it, and do not affirm it or deny it, but say: "We believe in what has been revealed to us and revealed to you."

﴿Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are submitting﴾. 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar informed us, 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Do not believe the People of the Book, nor deny them, but say: 'We believe in God and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter on what is permissible of explaining the Torah and others: 13/516, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/268. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/469.]]. Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us, 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us, Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafari informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, Ibn Abi Namlah al-Ansari informed us that his father, Abu Namlah al-Ansari, informed him: that while he was sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), a man from the Jews came to him, and a funeral passed by. He said: "O Muhammad, does this funeral speak?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God knows best." The Jew said: "It does speak." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whatever the People of the Book tell you, do not believe them nor deny them, but say: 'We believe in God, His books and His messengers. If it is false, you did not affirm it, and if it is true, you did not deny it'" [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 11/110; Abu Dawud in al-'Ilm, chapter on narrating the hadith of the People of the Book: 5/245, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. (58) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir: 22/349-351; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 2/10; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/136; and it was narrated by Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq.

Its origin is in al-Bukhari in abridged form from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (the preceding note). See also: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (128), al-Fath al-Samawi: 2/898-899, al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/469. Moreover, the Imam and Hafiz Ibn Kathir has scattered remarks regarding Isra'iliyyat and the narration from the People of the Book in his tafsir, which Shaykh Ahmad Muhammad Shakir collected in the introduction to his abridgement "'Umdat al-Tafsir": (1/14-19), which should be consulted.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 47–48:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: just as We sent the Scriptures to them, ﴿We have sent down to you the Book, and those whom We gave the Book believe in it﴾. This means: the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿And among these﴾, meaning: the people of Makkah, ﴿there are those who believe in it﴾, and they are the believers among the people of Makkah. ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾ (68/b). This is because the Jews recognized that Muhammad is a prophet and that the Qur'an is true, yet they denied it. Qatadah said: denial only occurs after recognition.

﴿And you did not recite﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿any Book before it﴾, before this Book was sent down to you, ﴿nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, meaning you did not write it. That is: you did not read or write before the revelation. ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt﴾. This means: if you had been writing or reading the Books before the revelation, the falsifiers, the polytheists of Makkah, would have doubted, and said: "He reads it from the books of the ancients and copies it from them." This was said by Qatadah. Muqatil said: "the falsifiers" are the Jews, and the meaning is: they would have doubted you and accused you, saying that the one whose description we find in the Torah is unlettered, who neither reads nor writes, and this man is not of that description.

[[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir (3/418) said: "That is: you have dwelt among your people, O Muhammad, before you brought this Qur'an, for a lifetime, not reading any book and not skilled in writing. Rather, every one of your people and others knows that you are an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes. Likewise is his description in the earlier Books, as Allah the Exalted said: 'Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel...' (the verse). Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained always, until the Day of Resurrection, unable to write; he did not write a single line or letter with his hand. Rather, he had scribes who wrote the revelation and the letters to the regions before him.

As for what some later jurists, such as the judge Abu al-Walid al-Baji and those who followed him, claimed, that he (peace be upon him) wrote on the day of Hudaybiyyah: "This is what Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah agreed to..." — what led them to this was a narration in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Then he took and wrote." This is to be understood in light of the other narration: "Then he commanded and it was written." For this reason, the jurists of the East and West strongly rejected the one who said the statement of al-Baji and disassociated themselves from it. What the man — I mean al-Baji — apparently intended is that he wrote that as a miracle, not that he was skilled at writing, as he (ﷺ) said, reporting about the Dajjal: "Written between his eyes: kafir," and in another narration: "K-F-R, which every believer will read." As for what some have cited, that he (ﷺ) did not die until he learned to write, it is weak and has no basis. See also: "al-Radd al-Shafi al-Wafir ʿala man nafa ummiyyat sayyid al-awwalin wa al-awakhir" by Ahmad ibn Hajar Al Ali. And refer to what precedes: 3/288; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz of Ibn ʿAtiyyah: 12/231.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 49–52:

﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.﴾ Al-Hasan said: It means the Qur'an is clear signs, ﴿in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, meaning the believers who have memorized the Qur'an. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father), and Qatadah said: ﴿Rather, he﴾ — meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) — is one possessing clear signs in the breasts of those among the People of the Book who have been given knowledge, because they find him described by his description and attributes in their scriptures. [[Al-Tabari mentioned both views (21/5–6) and preferred the view of the one who said: it means, "Rather, the knowledge that you did not recite any book before this one, nor write it with your right hand, are clear signs in the breasts of those among the People of the Book who have been given knowledge."

Because the saying of the Exalted, "Rather, it is clear signs…" falls between two reports from Allah about His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so making it a report about him is more appropriate than making it a report about the Book, about which the report was already concluded earlier.]] ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And they say: Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ Like what was sent down upon the prophets before him. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr read "āyah" in the singular; the others read "āyāt min rabbihi" in the plural. This is based on the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say: The signs are only with Allah﴾, the One Able to send them; if He wills, He sends them. ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾, warning the people of disobedience of the Fire, and the sending down of signs is not in my hand.

﴿Is it not sufficient for them﴾ — this is the answer to their saying, "Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord?" He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them?﴾ — meaning: Is the Qur'an, recited to them, not sufficient for them of the signs? ﴿Indeed in that﴾ — in the sending down of the Qur'an — ﴿is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾ That is: a reminder and an admonition for those who believe and act upon it.

﴿Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you﴾ that I am His Messenger and this Qur'an is His Book. ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood﴾ — Ibn 'Abbas said: in other than Allah. Muqatil said: in the worship of Satan — ﴿and disbelieve in Allah, those are the losers.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 49–52:

﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.﴾ Al-Hasan said: It means the Qur'an is clear signs, ﴿in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, meaning the believers who have memorized the Qur'an. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father), and Qatadah said: ﴿Rather, he﴾ — meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) — is one possessing clear signs in the breasts of those among the People of the Book who have been given knowledge, because they find him described by his description and attributes in their scriptures. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 29, verses 57–60:**

﴿Every soul shall taste death.﴾ He frightened them with death so that emigration (hijrah) would seem easier for them. That is: every one of them is subject to death wherever they are, so do not remain in the land of polytheism out of fear of death. ﴿Then to Us you will be returned.﴾ So We will recompense you for your deeds. Abu Bakr recited it as "yurja'un" (they will be returned) with the letter ya'.

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely settle them﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ta' (th) sakin, without a hamzah. It is said: "thawa al-rajul" (the man stayed) when he remained, and "athwaytuhu" (I made him stay) when I lodged him in a dwelling where he stays. The others read it with the letter ba' (b), with a fatha on it, a shaddah on the waw, and a hamzah after it, meaning: "lanunzilannahum" (We will surely lodge them). ﴿in the Garden, lofty chambers beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

﴿Those who were patient﴾ in hardships and did not abandon their religion because of severe trials that befell them, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is, they depend upon Him.

﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision﴾. The reason for this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the believers who were in Makkah, when the polytheists had harmed them: "Emigrate to Madinah." They said: "How can we leave for Madinah when we have no house or wealth there? Who will feed us and give us drink there?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And how many a creature﴾[[Ibn al-Jawzi reported it from Ibn 'Abbas without a chain: 6/282; al-Qurtubi: 13/360, which contains the weak hadith that follows.]] that has need of nourishment, ﴿does not carry its provision﴾, that is, it does not carry its sustenance with it and does not store anything for tomorrow, like the beasts and birds. ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾

wherever you are. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. All-Hearing of your words, (such as) "We do not find what we can spend in Madinah," and All-Knowing of what is in your hearts. Sufyan related from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar: "And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision," he said: "It does not store anything for tomorrow." Sufyan said: "Nothing among the creatures of Allah hoards except the human being, the mouse and the ant."[[See these reports in: al-Tabari: 21/11; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/475.]]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, Isma'il ibn Zurarah al-Raqqi informed us, Abu al-'Atuf al-Jarrah ibn Minhal informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ata' ibn Abi [69a] Rabah, from Ibn 'Umar who said: I entered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [an orchard of the orchards of the Ansar, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)][[What is between the brackets is missing from "a" (one manuscript).]] was picking dates with his hand and eating them. He said: "Eat, O Ibn 'Umar." I said: "I have no desire for them, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "But I have a desire for them. It is the fourth morning since I have eaten any food and found any." I said: "Indeed we belong to Allah; Allah is the One whose help is sought." He said: "O Ibn 'Umar, if I asked my Lord, He would give me the like of the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar many times over. But I go hungry one day and am satiated another day. So how will you be, O Ibn 'Umar, when you live long and remain among a worthless crowd of people who hoard a year's provision, and whose certainty weakens?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision﴾, to the end of the verse.[[Al-Suyuti attributed it (6/475) to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn 'Asakir with a weak chain. It was also reported by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 396–397. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (3/421): "This is a strange hadith, and Abu al-'Atuf al-Jazari is weak." Al-Qurtubi said (13/360): "This is weak; what refutes it is that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to store for his household the provision of a whole year" (agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim), "and the Companions used to do the same, and they are the exemplars, the people of certainty, and the leaders for those who came after them among the God-fearing and the reliant." Al-Shawkani said in Fath al-Qadir (4/213): "This hadith has severe objectionability, because it contradicts what the Prophet (peace be upon him) practiced, for he used to give his wives the provision of the year, as is established in the reliable books of hadith. Its chain includes Abu al-'Atuf al-Jazari, who is weak."]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us, Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Makhaladi informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): he did not store anything for the morrow.[[Al-Tirmidhi reported it in al-Zuhd, chapter "What has come concerning the living of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his family": 7/26, and said: "This is a strange hadith. Someone other than Ja'far ibn Sulayman has related it from Thabit from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a mursal." Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 2139, p. 525 of Mawarid al-Zaman. The author (al-Baghawi) cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/253. Al-Munawi said in Fayd al-Qadir (5/183): "The chain of the hadith is good. This hadith does not conflict with the earlier report that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to store a year's provision for his dependents. He did not store for himself, peace be upon him, but stored for others, such as his household, or he would have them own it and distribute it to them equally with others, as he would distribute to the Muslims what Allah gave him as fay'. And Allah knows best."]]

And we have related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If you truly put your trust in Allah, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they set out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening."[[Al-Tirmidhi reported it in al-Zuhd, chapter "What has come concerning asceticism in this world": 7/8, and said: "This is a good, sound hadith." Ibn Majah reported it in al-Zuhd, chapter "Trust and Certainty," no. 4164: 2/1394. Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 4/318. Ahmad reported it: 1/30, 52. The author cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/301.]]

Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Muzaffari informed us, Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih informed us, Abu Nasr ibn Hamduyah al-Mutawwi'i informed us, Abu al-Muwajjih Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, 'Abdan informed us, from Abu Hamzah, from Isma'il, that is Ibn Abi Khalid, from two men, one of whom was Zubayd al-Yami, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "O people, there is nothing that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have commanded you to it, and there is nothing that brings you closer to the Fire and distances you from Paradise except that I have forbidden you from it. Indeed the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril) has breathed into my heart that no soul will die until it has received its full provision. So fear Allah and seek provision in a good manner, and let the delay of provision not lead you to seek it through disobedience to Allah, for what is with Allah is not attained except through obedience to Him."[[Al-Hakim reported it: 2/4, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/303–304. Al-Haythami (sic: the Mishkat, 3/1458) attributed it to al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 64–67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play.﴾ Al-lahw (amusement) is: enjoying the pleasures of this world, and al-la'ib (play) is: frivolity. They are so called because it is perishable.

﴿And indeed, the Last Abode – that is the (true) life.﴾ That is: the lasting, everlasting life. Al-hayawan (life) has the meaning of al-hayah (life), i.e., therein is everlasting life. ﴿If only they knew.﴾ [They would know] the perishing of this world and the enduring of the Hereafter.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ – and they abandon the idols – ﴿but when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.﴾ This is a report about their obstinacy, and that in times of hardship they acknowledge that the One Able to remove it is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, alone; but when it passes, they return to their disbelief. ʿIkrimah said: When the people of the Jahiliyyah boarded the sea, they would carry idols with them; when the wind grew fierce upon them, they would cast them into the sea and say, "O Lord, O Lord."

﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾ – this is the lam of command, and its meaning is threat and warning, like His saying: "Do what you will" [Fussilat: 40]; that is, that they may deny the blessing of Allah in His saving them. ﴿And that they may enjoy themselves﴾ – Hamzah and al-Kisai read it with a sukun on the lam, while the rest read it with a kasrah, coordinated with His saying "so that they may deny." ﴿But they will soon know.﴾ It has been said: whoever reads the lam with a kasrah takes it as the lam of purpose (lam kay), and likewise in liyakfuru; the meaning is that they gain nothing from associating partners except disbelief and enjoying what they enjoy in this world, without any share in the Hereafter.

﴿Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ That is, the Arabs, where some of them take others captive, while the people of Makkah are secure. ﴿Then in falsehood – in the idols and Satan – do they believe, and in the favor of Allah – in Muhammad and Islam – do they disbelieve?﴾
